cover.hook: $4.7B in VIA Rail manufacturing lands at Thunder Bay's Alstom plant.
cover.sub: Plus: Anthropic cuts cache costs 75%, GPT-6 Astra crosses the critical cyber threshold, Canada launches a new AI agency, and a federal consultation closes September 23.

reelSub: $4.7B Via Rail in Thunder Bay, Claude Fable 5.1 cuts costs 75%, GPT-6 Astra hits the critical cyber threshold, and Canada launches Digital Transformation Canada.
storySub: Five moves this week that matter for NWO businesses and governments watching AI and infrastructure.

items.title: $4.7B Via Rail deal: 313 passenger cars built at Thunder Bay's Alstom plant
items.body: PM Carney announced September 3 at the Thunder Bay Alstom plant. 313 new cars, first made-in-Canada in ~40 years, ~700 jobs in Ontario and Quebec. First delivery 2031.
items.reelLine: PM Carney announced a $4.7B Via Rail contract at Thunder Bay's Alstom plant on September 3 — 313 cars, first made-in-Canada in 40 years.

items.title: Anthropic Fable 5.1: cache-read costs drop 75%
items.body: Cache reads fall from $1.00 to $0.25 per million tokens. Anthropic estimates 25-45% effective cost reduction depending on workload. Agentic benchmarks also jumped sharply.
items.tease: Next: OpenAI's most capable model yet.
items.reelLine: Claude Fable 5.1 launched September 1 with cache-read costs 75% lower — a significant cut for NWO businesses running on the Claude API.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra: OpenAI's first model to hit the critical cyber threshold
items.body: Released September 3. OpenAI designated Astra as its first model capable of exploiting previously unknown vulnerabilities in well-protected systems. Greg Brockman called it a possible start of AGI.
items.reelLine: GPT-6 Astra launched September 3 — the first OpenAI model to cross the critical cybersecurity threshold under its preparedness framework.

items.title: Digital Transformation Canada launches under ex-Google CFO Patrick Pichette
items.body: New federal agency combines Shared Services Canada with three other departments. Will direct government procurement toward Canadian AI companies and run a private-sector AI fellowship.
items.tease: Next: Canada's AI transparency window is closing.
items.reelLine: Ottawa launched Digital Transformation Canada on September 3 under Patrick Pichette — federal procurement shifting toward Canadian AI and tech firms.

items.title: Canada's AI transparency consultation closes September 23 — two weeks left
items.body: ISED is still accepting comments on how Canada discloses AI interactions and AI-generated content. Email AIConsultations-ConsultationsIA@ised-isde.gc.ca before September 23.
items.reelLine: Canada's AI transparency consultation closes September 23 — two weeks left to submit a regional perspective to ISED.

summary.title: A $4.7B manufacturing deal in Thunder Bay and a federal AI push — Canada moved fast this week
summary.body: PM Carney made the largest VIA Rail investment in history at the Thunder Bay Alstom plant, while Ottawa simultaneously launched a new digital transformation agency and two major AI model releases landed from Anthropic and OpenAI. The through-line is federal scale: Canada is spending and structuring for AI-era infrastructure, and NWO sits at the intersection of manufacturing, power, and a federal AI strategy still open for comment until September 23.

captions.carousel: This week in Northwestern Ontario: PM Carney announced a $4.7B VIA Rail manufacturing contract at Thunder Bay's Alstom plant — 313 new passenger cars, the first made in Canada in roughly 40 years, supporting nearly 700 jobs. Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 with cache-read costs 75% lower — a direct cost cut for NWO businesses running on the Claude API. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra crossed the critical cybersecurity threshold under its preparedness framework. Ottawa launched Digital Transformation Canada under former Google CFO Patrick Pichette, directing federal procurement toward Canadian AI companies. And Canada's AI transparency consultation closes September 23 — there are still two weeks to submit a regional perspective to ISED.
